This workaround did the trick for me.

Thank you very much!

messages.subject: How to read .sql files in R
messages.subject_clean: How to read .sql files in R
messages.body_plain:
Dear sqldf users,

I use R for my statistic analysis. I've got several .sql files countaining the data of an experiment, and I want to read this data with R. The data that I try to read are distributed in several table into the sql file (table : answers, users, ...) and I need to bind these different data tables in order to build a set of data suitable for data analysis (for example, categorical data from 'users' table need to match with data from 'answers' table). I've loaded sqldf package, updated R (version 3.1.2) and red how to write sql statments. I tried to read my sql files with sqldf and read.csv.sql functions, but unfortunately got nothing else that these kind of error outputs :

read.csv.sql('file.sql', sql="SELECT * FROM users")
Error in sqliteSendQuery(con, statement, bind.data) :
  error in statement: no such table: users

(I've tried a lot of other syntaxes and adding arguments to the function without success...)

Do somebody have an idea of how to do that?

Many thanks!

Florian

messages.body_plain:

Thanks,

Peter

messages.subject: Re: comment.char argument disappeared from read.csv.sql (?)
messages.body_plain:
comment.char seemed to be involved in one of the incompatabilities with the new RSQLite 1.0.0 and has been removed in order not to hold up 0.4-10 until I find the time to track it down.

You can use the filter argument in the interim, e.g.

     read.csq.sql(...whatever..., filter = 'sed -e "s/ *#.*//" ')

(If you are on Windows note that sed is available in Rtools.)

That example using filter should be exactly equivalent to using comment.char="#".  Note that it is not a new feature.  sqldf has had the filter argument for quite some time, maybe years.

If you can wait a bit I do intend to put the comment.char feature back but I was concerned that it was holding up all uses of read.csv.sql so at least now it works as before in most cases and there is the indicated workaround for anyone who needs to remove comments.

messages.subject: Re: comment.char argument disappeared from read.csv.sql (?)
messages.body_plain: Just a follow up.  I have looked into it a bit and the comment.char argument that was in prior versions of sqldf was passed to RSQLite but RSQLite did not actually do anything with it -- RSQLite's import  functionality never had the capability to remove comments.  Thus the main change that has caused problems seems to be just that RSQLite no longer accepts arguments that it does not implement.  When using sqldf the way to remove comments is by using the filter= argument and it seems that this was always the case.  Should RSQLite implement a comment.char in the future then I hope to provide this in sqldf as well.
